summary: A lookout cabin built around 1942 on Castle Mountain in Banff National Park; the cabin is gone and only its foundation remains, reached by a 3.7 km trail.

facts.design: Lookout cabin on the mountain slope
facts.status_note: The cabin is gone; a hiking guide says only the foundation of the former lookout remains.

access.note: A hiking trail in Banff National Park runs from the Bow Valley Parkway to the former lookout site.

visit.trail_note: 3.7 km one way from the Bow Valley Parkway, a steady climb through dense forest; carry bear spray.

events.note: Crag & Canyon (Banff) reported on October 31, 1941 that the top of Castle Mountain had been chosen for a lookout
Lookout cabin constructed around 1942, per the Kemnow page and the hiking guide
Mountain renamed in honour of General Dwight D. Eisenhower, per the Kemnow page; hiking guides still use Castle Mountain
Hiking guide: by 1978 all of the park's lookouts had been torn down or abandoned; the guide gives no separate date for this cabin

notes_for_editor: The 1941 notice and the c.1942 build come from the Kemnow page, which cites Crag & Canyon and Mike Potter's 1998 guide; neither original was read. The 1946 rename rests on the Kemnow page alone. The 1941 notice names the top of the mountain, but the hiking guide puts the built cabin less than halfway up; the sources do not explain the difference, so the story says so. The 'by 1978' line is a general claim about the park's lookouts, not a dated removal for this cabin. The brief's agency (Parks Canada) is not stated in any source read, so it is left out of facts; the sources mention Parks Canada only for trail conditions and rules. The Kemnow page lists the lookout as 'Removed' with no date. Access: no closure found; trail is public per the guide. Parks Canada's own pages were not checked.
